children: Gold futures recover losses that followed the Fed's rate hike as Treasury yields move lower and the dollar slips, while oil prices extend their pullback to a second day. "Gold is rangebound with two-way risk, but the large bull market we had seen earlier in the year is considered on pause for now," Pepperstone strategist Ahmad Assiri says in a note. The bull market could continue at some stage with underlying drivers such as central bank demand, macro uncertainty, and fiscal concerns, he says. But "the path of oil prices and their transmission into Fed policy remains the single most important variable from now till year-end." The December contract is up 0.4% in New York at $4,404.90 a troy ounce. Silver rises 2.3% to $66.44 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
